chunks: The report of Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about shortening, so he said
"A barid going and a barid returning. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he came to Dhuباب, shortened."

key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: a postal measure of travel distance used here as the legal standard
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice establishes the sunnah

ai.seo_question: What travel distance requires shortening the prayer in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal measure for qaṣr in travel prayer as a barid outbound and a barid inbound. It also supports the ruling through the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating the sunnah basis for shortening salat during travel.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1303 - Jamil ibn Darraj reported from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (as) about the ruling for shortening the prayer.
Imam (as) said: "A barid going and a barid returning. The Messenger of Allah (sw) would shorten his prayers when he reached Dhu'bāb."
